content.one_sentence_role: Selects a maximizing dual frame for a specified basis.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space, and fix an ordered basis $b=(b_j)_{j=1}^n$. Write $C_b:E\to\mathbb R^n$ for the coordinate isomorphism, defined by $x=\sum_{j=1}^n(C_bx)_j b_j$, and give its coordinate space the sup norm $\|c\|_\infty=\max_j|c_j|$ (zero in dimension zero). A frame is an ordered family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ of continuous real linear functionals, with no independence assumed. Its matrix and evaluation map are
$$M_F=(\ell_i(b_j))_{i,j},\qquad T_Fx=(\ell_i(x))_i=M_FC_bx.$$
The admissible frames form the product of closed dual unit balls
$$\mathcal U=\{F:\|\ell_i\|_{E^*}\le1\text{ for every }i\}.$$
The norm on $E$ need not be a coordinate sup norm. There is a frame $F_*\in\mathcal U$ such that
$$\forall F\in\mathcal U,\quad |\det M_F|\le|\det M_{F_*}|.$$
content.assumptions: The space is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb R$ and $b$ is its specified basis indexed by $n$ elements. Each admissible row lies in the closed operator unit ball. No independence of the varying frames, positive dimension, or uniqueness of a maximizing frame is assumed.
content.conclusion: One admissible frame attains the maximum of the absolute determinant. The numerical maximum $D_b=|\det M_{F_*}|$ depends on $b$, although its value does not depend on which maximizer is chosen. Positivity is a separate result.
content.proof_summary: Use compactness of the finite product of dual balls and continuity of the absolute determinant.

proof_steps.text:
**Supply the compact domain.** The dual space $E^*$ is finite-dimensional, hence its closed unit ball $\overline B_{E^*}(0,1)$ is compact. The [compact dual unit ball](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L125-L128) and [finite product of these balls](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L130-L136) give
   $$\mathcal U=\prod_{i=1}^n \overline B_{E^*}(0,1)\quad\text{compact}.$$
   The [zero-frame witness](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L138-L141) is $\ell_i=0$ for every $i$, so the domain is nonempty, also when $n=0$.

**Maximize the correct function.** Every entry $F\mapsto\ell_i(b_j)$ is continuous, and the determinant is a finite sum of products of entries. Therefore $F\mapsto|\det M_F|$ is continuous, as in [continuity of the frame determinant](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L116-L123). Apply the extreme-value theorem to this continuous real function on the nonempty compact set $\mathcal U$. Its output is $F_*\in\mathcal U$ with the displayed comparison for every $F\in\mathcal U$. This is an absolute maximum; no sign of $\det M_{F_*}$ is asserted.

content.lean_realization_notes: The selected maximizer is named by [the choice of maximizing frame](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L152-L154) and its value by [the attained maximum](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L167-L169). The coordinate identity $T_F=M_FC_b$ is [evaluation in basis coordinates](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L99-L114). These names do not add uniqueness or a nonzero determinant to this theorem.
